title: FileNotFoundError
kicker: Python for SDFs · Fix the error
code:
import json
with open("/content/sdf-dates.json") as f:
    dates = json.load(f)
print(dates)
traceback: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/content/sdf-dates.json'

notes.label: FileNotFoundError
notes.text: The type of error. Python looked for a file at that exact path and found nothing there.

notes.label: [Errno 2] No such file or directory
notes.text: The same news from the operating system. Errno 2 is its code for a missing file.

notes.label: '/content/sdf-dates.json'
notes.text: The path Python tried. Compare it letter by letter with Colab's Files panel, where the upload is called sdf_dates.json, with underscores. If the names match, check the file is still there: uploads disappear when the runtime resets.

fixes.label: with open("/content/sdf_dates.json") as f:
fixes.title: Best fix
fixes.feedback: The path now matches the uploaded file, sdf_dates.json, exactly, so the cell loads it and prints the dates. The safest way to get a path right is to right-click the file in the Files panel, choose Copy path, and paste it.
fixes.fixed_code:
# Test fixture, not shown to students: in Colab this file exists because you uploaded it.
import os, json
os.makedirs("/content", exist_ok=True)
with open("/content/sdf_dates.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(["2023-04-12", "2021-09-30"], f)
# The fixed cell:
import json
with open("/content/sdf_dates.json") as f:
    dates = json.load(f)
print(dates)

fixes.label: with open("sdf-dates.json") as f:
fixes.title: Still a FileNotFoundError
fixes.feedback: Colab starts in the /content folder, so leaving it out changes nothing. The name still has dashes where the real file has underscores.
fixes.fixed_code:
import json
with open("sdf-dates.json") as f:
    dates = json.load(f)
print(dates)

fixes.label: with open("/content/sdf-dates.json", "w") as f:
fixes.title: A new error, and a new empty file
fixes.feedback: `"w"` opens a file for writing. Python creates an empty sdf-dates.json, and then `json.load` fails because a file opened for writing can't be read.
fixes.fixed_code:
import json
with open("/content/sdf-dates.json", "w") as f:
    dates = json.load(f)
print(dates)
